newsitem.title: INDIA: India says its envoys in Kabul left just in time.
newsitem.headline: India says its envoys in Kabul left just in time.

text.p: India said on Friday it was watching the "extremely fluid situation" in Afghanistan and disclosed that its diplomats had been evacuated from Kabul just hours before the city fell to the invading Taleban militia.
Foreign Secretary Salman Haider told a news conference that 11 Indian officials left on the last flight from the Bagram military airbase near Kabul on Thursday night.
"We are watching an extremely fluid situation which is very unclear," Haider, India's top diplomat, said.
A 10-member team of Indian doctors and technicians running a medical clinic in Kabul were evacuated on Monday, he said.
"Our understanding is that the only diplomats remaining there were from Indonesia, Iran and Turkey," he said.

India's response to the fall of Kabul to the Islamic rebels was subdued, compared with its condemnation of what it said were Pakistan-backed Islamic groups when they attacked Afghan President Burhanuddin Rabbani's troops in October last year.
Indian charge d'affaires in Afghanistan Azad Singh Toor said Kabul was very tense after the town of Sarobi, just northeast of Kabul, fell to the Taleban on Tuesday.
"That was the deadliest blow," Toor said. "There were heavy civilian casualties in Kabul due to (Taleban) artillery shelling for the last several days."
India's relations with Afghanistan soured after former president Najibullah's communist government fell in April 1992.
But New Delhi revived diplomatic ties in May 1995 when Toor reopened the mission in the Afghan capital.
Taleban leaders said Najibullah and his brother Shahpur Ahmadzai were executed after the militia took over Kabul.
Haider said Najibullah's widow Fattan and their three daughters were safe in New Delhi.
Asked if the situation in Afghanistan affected India, Haider said: "A settled Afghanistan could provide potential access to Central Asia."
Afghanistan's ambassador to India said on Friday that Rabbani and members of his collapsed government were about 25 km (15 miles) north of Kabul.
